focus: weighted interpolation, factorization, ramification cleanup, and characteristic-safe propagation

messages.body_markdown: The audit of researcher-0007 upheld the factorwise $\Xi_i$ and polar calculations, but its overall verdict is `revise`, so AE-17 remains provisional. The required mathematical wording is $C_Z\ne0$; $\deg_ZC<p$ is only a sufficient condition. Use the exact P1--P5 triples, but do not promote them to verified progress.
messages.subject: Factorwise polar audit landed

messages.body_markdown: Confirmed, with a weaker algebraic handoff than previously requested: if $\Omega_\eta(\epsilon)$ accepted edge mass lies on a rank-reaching relation of weight $D\le K_\eta d$, then factorwise cleanup costs $O_\eta(d/p)$, at most $K_\eta$ factors remain, and averaging gives a simple seed with more than the factor weight in compatible directions. AE-26 and AE-21 then aggregate one $Q$ globally without connectivity, minimum-degree inheritance, or Vinh mixing.
messages.subject: Total-mass bounded-weight interface

messages.body_markdown: AE-26 isolates the requested standalone lemma. At a simple lift, take the formal implicit root, truncate it to total degree $d$, and use uniqueness to identify its restriction with every supplied line polynomial. Then $C(X,Y,Q)$ has degree at most $\Delta$ and more than $\Delta$ distinct line factors, so it is zero; irreducibility gives $C\sim Z-Q$. Researcher-0007:P6 supports the Newton mechanism but has a `revise` audit, while researcher-0002:P8 proves only component decoding. A fresh exact audit is still required.
messages.subject: Standalone factor linearization

messages.body_markdown: The bounded-weight route removes the whole-line minimum-degree requirement from my earlier request. Incidence need only retain $\Omega_\eta(\epsilon)$ total accepted edge mass on the lines of the rank-reaching relation; AE-17--AE-20 localize that mass and manufacture the high-direction seed by averaging. The direct-decode branch remains essential because fixed-$\theta$ graph-only covers can still cost $\Omega_\theta(p/\epsilon)$.
messages.subject: Relaxed incidence handoff

nodes.label: Accepted-incidence instance
nodes.notes: This fixes the bivariate prime-field campaign regime and normalization.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $100<d<p$, a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and polynomials $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ with $\deg P_L\le d$ for every affine line $L$. Put $$E_{\mathrm{acc}}=\{(x,L):x\in L,\ P_L(x)=f(x)\},\qquad \mu(E)=\frac{|E|}{p^2(p+1)},\qquad \epsilon=\mu(E_{\mathrm{acc}}),$$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=\max_{\deg Q\le d}\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)].$$

nodes.label: Weighted rank-reaching relation
nodes.notes: The rank condition measures labeled graph constraints rather than the cardinality of a line selector.
nodes.statement_markdown: For an integer $D\ge d$, give $X,Y,Z$ weights $1,1,d$ and put $$V_D=\{A:\operatorname{wdeg}A\le D\},\qquad N_d(D)=\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor D/d\rfloor}\binom{D-dj+2}{2}.$$ For $R$ a line family, define $$\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\to\bigoplus_{M\in R}\mathbb F_p[t]_{\le D},\qquad A\mapsto\bigl(A(M(t),P_M(t))\bigr)_{M\in R}.$$ For an accepted graph $G=(X,T,E)$, let $$\operatorname{Reach}_R(L)=\{x:(x,L)\in E,\ \exists M\in R\setminus\{L\},\ (x,M)\in E\}.$$ The tuple $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching if $R\subseteq T$, $|R|>D$, $\operatorname{rank}\Phi_{R,D}<N_d(D)$, and $|\operatorname{Reach}_R(L)|>D$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Algebra-ready core
nodes.notes: This remains the interface for the accepted component-level route.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $0<\epsilon\le1$ and $a>0$, an $(\epsilon,a)$-core is an accepted graph $G=(X,T,E)$ satisfying $$\mu(E)\ge a\epsilon,\qquad \min_{v\in X\sqcup T}\deg_G(v)\ge\lfloor a\epsilon p\rfloor.$$

nodes.label: Constant-loss core pruning
nodes.notes: The exact source audit has verdict `revise`; the harness therefore keeps this import provisional.
nodes.statement_markdown: Every accepted graph of mass $\epsilon$ contains a subgraph of mass at least $\epsilon/4$ and minimum degree at least $\lfloor\epsilon p/100\rfloor$.

nodes.label: Component measures
nodes.notes: This starts the exact accepted component decoder.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $G=(X,T,E)$ be connected with minimum degree $k$, let $\tau=|T|/[p(p+1)]$, and put $C_*=2^{40}$. If $$k^2\ge C_*dp,\qquad k^3\ge C_*d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\frac{|X|}{p^2}\ge\frac{k}{4p},\qquad \tau\ge\frac{k}{4p}.$$

nodes.label: Component-sensitive reaching family
nodes.notes: Distinct target-line points depend on disjoint choices of other affine lines.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under AE-05, writing $t=|T|$, there is $R\subseteq T$ such that $$\frac{4t}{k}\le |R|\le\frac{16t}{k},\qquad |\operatorname{Reach}_R(L)|>\frac12\deg_G(L)\quad(L\in T),$$ and $|R|\ge p+1$.

nodes.label: Weighted squarefree interpolant
nodes.notes: This is ordinary weighted interpolation, not multiplicity interpolation.
nodes.statement_markdown: Set $$D=16\bigl(\lfloor\sqrt{d|R|}\rfloor+1\bigr).$$ There is a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ such that $A_Z\ne0$ and $$A(M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0\quad(M\in R).$$ Moreover, $$D^2\le\frac{32768d\tau p^2}{k},\qquad \frac Dk<\frac1{5000},\qquad D<k\le p<|R|.$$

nodes.label: Linewise identity extension
nodes.notes: The transfer uses more than $D$ distinct accepted roots on each target line.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every $L\in T$, $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$

nodes.label: Content and resultant cleanup
nodes.notes: The accepted source uses a coprime formal directional derivative and no discriminant.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient gcd in $Z$. Then $B$ is primitive, squarefree, $Z$-dependent, and of degree below $p$. There is a formal directional derivative $\mathcal D$ with $\gcd(B,\mathcal DB)=1$ and an exceptional set satisfying $$|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|\le pD^2+D|T|.$$ Outside $E_{\mathrm{exc}}$, the $B$-graph identity holds and $\mathcal DB(x,f(x))\ne0$.

nodes.label: Surviving clean core
nodes.notes: The peeling may disconnect the graph.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under AE-05--AE-09, $$\frac{|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|}{|E|}\le\frac Dk+ rac{16384dp}{k^2}<\frac1{4000}.$$ Peeling below $k_1=\lfloor k/100\rfloor$ leaves a nonempty accepted graph of minimum degree at least $k_1$.

nodes.label: Vertical simplicity from two directions
nodes.notes: Two distinct affine lines through one point have independent base directions in dimension two.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Every point vertex $x$ of the graph left by AE-10 satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Accepted component decoder
nodes.notes: Newton lifting divides only by certified nonzero values of $B_Z$ and returns one polynomial.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under AE-05--AE-11, there exists $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{k}{800p}.$$

nodes.label: Conditional square-root frontier
nodes.notes: The source status is `conditional`; the unresolved premise is the small line measure of a pruned component.
nodes.statement_markdown: If a standard pruned core has a connected component of line measure at most $\Lambda\epsilon$ and $$\epsilon\ge\sqrt{8{,}000{,}000\cdot2^{40}\Lambda}\left(\frac dp\right)^{1/2},$$ then some total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial has agreement at least $\epsilon/160000$.

nodes.label: Whole-explainer square-root floor
nodes.notes: This diagnoses the accepted architecture, not every algebraic method.
nodes.statement_markdown: In AE-05--AE-12, $$D=\Theta\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{d\tau p^2}{k}}\right),\qquad D<k.$$ Since $\tau\ge k/(4p)$, these conditions force $k^2=\Omega(dp)$; with $k=\Theta(\epsilon p)$, this route cannot close below $\epsilon=\Omega((d/p)^{1/2})$.

nodes.label: Universal-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: A smaller universal reaching family must be accompanied by a decoder alternative.
nodes.statement_markdown: For suitable integers $K$ there are legal constant-label tables with $1/(2K)\le\epsilon\le2/K$ such that every line family reaching half of every accepted line has $$|R|\ge\frac{p}{32\epsilon},$$ while a constant polynomial has agreement at least $\epsilon/2$.

nodes.label: Uniform-jet rank-blind barrier
nodes.notes: The audit is inexact with verdict `revise`. This applies only to raw coefficient counting and uniform graph-ideal multiplicity; sparse or dependent jets remain open.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $s,D,n,h$ be positive integers with $d\le D<p$ and $n>D$. Put $$C_s(D,d)=\sum_{a+b<s}\max(D-a-db+1,0).$$ If $$N_d(D)>nC_s(D,d),\qquad sh>D,$$ then $$h^2>\frac{dn}{12}.$$

nodes.label: Bounded-weight rank-or-decode handoff
nodes.notes: This is the principal open incidence obligation. AE-14 rules out replacing it by a uniformly smaller graph-only cover.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $0<\eta<1$ there exist constants $C_\eta,a_\eta>0$ and $K_\eta\ge1$ such that, whenever $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\eta},$$ either there exists a total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial $Q$ with $\Pr[Q=f]\ge a_\eta\epsilon$, or there are an accepted graph $G=(X,T,E)$, $R\subseteq T$, and an integer $D$ satisfying $$\mu(E)\ge a_\eta\epsilon,\qquad d\le D\le K_\eta d,$$ for which $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching.

nodes.label: Near-linear parameter slack
nodes.notes: The bound follows from $D/(\epsilon p)\le K_\eta(d/p)^\eta/C_\eta$ and from $\epsilon\le1$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
After increasing $C_\eta$ as a function of $a_\eta,K_\eta,\eta$, every relation alternative of AE-18 satisfies $$D<p,
\qquad
\frac Dp\le\frac{a_\eta}{100K_\eta}\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Squarefree rank-kernel relation
nodes.notes: Rank deficiency gives a kernel element; taking the product of its distinct irreducible factors preserves every selected graph identity. The condition $|R|>D$ excludes a pure-content relation.
nodes.statement_markdown:
In the relation alternative there exists a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ such that $$A_Z\ne0,
\qquad
A(M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0\quad(M\in R).$$

nodes.label: Reached-root extension
nodes.notes: This is the accepted linewise root-count argument instantiated with the rank-reaching family.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every line vertex $L\in T$, $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$

nodes.label: Primitive factor allocation
nodes.notes: Allocation uses that a product restriction vanishing in $\mathbb F_p[t]$ has a vanishing factor restriction.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient gcd in $Z$, $h=\deg H$, and $\delta=\operatorname{wdeg}B$. Delete the at most $h$ lines on which $H$ vanishes identically. Then $B$ is primitive, squarefree, and $Z$-dependent, and $$B=c\prod_{i=1}^s C_i,
\qquad
s\le\deg_ZB\le\frac\delta d\le\frac Dd\le K_\eta.$$ The remaining lines admit a disjoint allocation $T=\bigsqcup_iT_i$ satisfying $$C_i(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0\quad(L\in T_i).$$

nodes.label: Factorwise separability and polar cleanup
nodes.notes: The researcher-0006 backbone is accepted. The exact factorwise aggregation from researcher-0007 has an exact audit but overall verdict `revise`, so this node remains provisional. The exact derivative condition is $C_{i,Z}\ne0$; $\delta<p$ is sufficient.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For each factor put $$\delta_i=\operatorname{wdeg}C_i,
\quad r_i=\deg_ZC_i,
\quad \gamma_i=\operatorname{wdeg}(C_{i,Z}),$$ and $$\Xi_i=(r_i-1)\delta_i+r_i\gamma_i-dr_i(r_i-1).$$ Since $\delta\le D<p$, every $C_i$ satisfies $\gcd(C_i,C_{i,Z})=1$. Delete each identically $C_{i,Z}$-ramified line and every accepted incidence with $C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))=0$. If $\tau_i=|T_i|/[p(p+1)]$, $\tau=\sum_i\tau_i$, and $\bar\delta=\tau^{-1}\sum_i\tau_i\delta_i$, then the total deleted mass, including content lines, is at most $$\beta\le\frac{D^2/d-D}{p(p+1)}+ rac{\tau(\bar\delta-d)}p.$$ Every remaining edge assigned to $i$ satisfies $C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))\ne0$.

nodes.label: Heavy clean factor and simple seed
nodes.notes: This uses total accepted mass only; no inherited line degree, connectivity, or incidence mixing is needed.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Under AE-23 and AE-17, the clean factor classes have total mass at least $a_\eta\epsilon/2$. Hence some class has mass $$
u_i\ge rac{a_\eta}{2K_\eta}\epsilon.$$ Moreover, $$
u_i(p+1)>\delta_i,$$ so there exists a point $b$ incident to more than $\delta_i$ distinct clean lines of $T_i$, all satisfying $$C_i(b,f(b))=0,
\qquad
C_{i,Z}(b,f(b))
e0.$$

nodes.label: Simple-pencil factor linearization
nodes.notes: At the simple lift, construct the formal implicit root and truncate it to total degree $d$. Its restriction equals every supplied $P_L$ by uniqueness. No accepted exact source currently proves this standalone package.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $C\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be irreducible with $\Delta=\operatorname{wdeg}C$. Suppose $C_Z(b,z)\ne0$ and more than $\Delta$ distinct affine lines $L$ through $b$ admit polynomials $P_L$ of degree at most $d$ satisfying $$P_L(b)=z,
\qquad
C(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$ Then there exists $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$C(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\equiv0,
\qquad
C\sim Z-Q.$$

nodes.label: Vinh-free global aggregation
nodes.notes: All disconnected pieces assigned to the same irreducible factor charge to the same polynomial.
nodes.statement_markdown: Applying AE-26 to the seed from AE-20 gives one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial $Q$ such that $Q(x)=f(x)$ at every endpoint of the clean factor class. Consequently, $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\nu_i\ge\frac{a_\eta}{2K_\eta}\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Near-linear algebraic propagation engine
nodes.notes: No submission proves this theorem. It is blocked principally on AE-18 and on fresh accepted audits of AE-17 and AE-26.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $0<\eta<1$ there exist constants $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, every integer $100<d<p$, and every legal bivariate line-versus-point instance, $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\eta}$$ implies the existence of one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Fallback heavy-factor or cross-factor decoder
nodes.notes: This is off the critical path when AE-18 supplies $D=O_\eta(d)$. It is needed if the factor count grows with $\epsilon^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Suppose instead that the relation handoff only gives $$D\le A_\eta d\epsilon^{-\eta/(1-\eta)}.$$ Then either one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial has agreement at least $b_\eta\epsilon$, or some cleaned factor class satisfies $$\nu_i\ge b_\eta\epsilon,
\qquad
\nu_i(p+1)>\delta_i.$$

nodes.label: Singular-lift guardrail
nodes.notes: This is not a soundness counterexample; it shows that absolute irreducibility and many graph lines cannot replace a simple common lift.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every prime $p$ and $101\le d\le p-2$, there exist $D=d+1<p$, a primitive squarefree absolutely irreducible polynomial $B$ of weighted degree $D$, and more than $D$ degree-at-most-$d$ graph lines, each containing a singular ramified lift, such that no total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial matches all the selected line labels.

summary: The exact accepted corpus still provides the full component-level chain from weighted interpolation through characteristic-safe cleanup and recovery of one polynomial, but its degree and support budgets stop at a square-root frontier. Round 2 therefore pivots to a bounded-weight rank-or-decode handoff: preserve constant accepted mass and obtain a rank-reaching relation with $D\le K_\eta d$. Rank deficiency gives a squarefree relation, reached-root counting extends it to every carrier line, and factorwise resultant accounting deletes only $O_\eta(d/p)$ mass. Since at most $K_\eta$ factors remain, one clean factor retains $\Omega_\eta(\epsilon)$ mass; averaging supplies a simple point with more compatible directions than the factor weight. A characteristic-safe formal implicit-root argument then forces that irreducible factor to be $Z-Q$, and all its edges aggregate to the same global $Q$ without connectivity or Vinh mixing. The old heavy-factor dichotomy is now only a fallback for unbounded $D/d$. The main rank-or-decode handoff is open, the factorwise audit remains revise-grade, and the standalone factor-linearization lemma still needs an accepted exact audit.
target_statement: Prove an algebraic interpolation-and-propagation lemma strong enough to preserve a near-linear power of the accepted incidence density over $\mathbb F_p^2$.
title: Algebraic propagation engine
